title: Fusion-stride profiling labbook: Flash vs paged vs fused-stride-v2
content:
Purpose:
This labbook captures a set of microbench experiments comparing: FlashAttention (reference upstream build), PagedAttention (our paged-KV approach), and a new fused kernel prototype (fused-stride-v2) that attempts to interleave softmax+scale+matmul into a single pass to reduce global memory traffic. The goal: measure throughput/latency tradeoffs and identify workload patterns where fused-stride-v2 gives win or regressions versus Flash.

Background/hypotheses (quick):
- FlashAttention is extremely bandwidth- and register-efficient for contiguous KV layouts but assumes full sequence fits into working memory patterns.
- Paged attention reduces peak memory by spilling KV pages; expected to help long-context workloads at cost of extra loads/indirection.
- Fused-stride-v2 aims to reduce intermediate writes for fused softmax + scaling + writeback; hypothesis is better latency for small-medium seq lengths (<= 2048) and improved p99 by reducing memory stalls, but may underutilize TensorCores on certain shapes.

Experiment rigs and baseline config:
- Hardware: 1x A100 40GB (prod-sim runner), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS 12, PyTorch 2.2.0-nightly (patched), Nsight/System and nvprof for micro traces.
- Software builds:
  - flash-ref: upstream flashattention@v2.0 commit 1a3f7b (build with -O3, fp16 kernels enabled)
  - paged-opt: internal paged-attn branch paged-kv-opt commit b4e6d2 (our paging allocator + async prefetch)
  - fused-stride-v2: prototype branch fused-stride-v2 commit c9d2e0 (hand-written cuda kernel with fused softmax+scale kernel; experimental shared memory tiling)
- Models / shapes:
  - encoder-like: batch 2 x seq 512 x heads 32 x head_dim 64 (typical embed 4096)
  - long-context: batch 1 x seq 8192 x heads 16 x head_dim 64 (paged scenario)
  - chat-medium: batch 1 x seq 2048 (prefix 128, generation 1920) with incremental KV cache + micro-batching of 4 requests
- Measurement: tokens/sec throughput (steady-state >= 60s runs), median & p99 latency per generate call, GPU memory (resident), SM/TensorCore utilization (Nsight), L2 read/write bytes (cuda profiler).

Microbench steps (repro):
1) Warm up: 30 iterations single-thread warmup for each kernel/shape.
2) Steady run: 500 iterations measure mean tokens/sec.
3) p99: capture latencies per iteration and compute 99th percentile.
4) Collect traces: nvprof timeline for a 20-iteration window capturing kernel timelines and memcopy overlap.

Key observations (summary):
- encoder-like (seq512): flash-ref achieves best overall throughput: 1.00x baseline. fused-stride-v2 shows +6-9% throughput improvement on mean latency but p99 slightly worse (+8%) in some runs due to occasional shared-memory bank conflicts seen in kernel-level traces. paged-opt is ~0.85x (expected overhead of page indirection).
- long-context (seq8192): paged-opt clearly wins in memory footprint (resident ~22GB vs flash-ref OOM). Throughput is lower than flash-ref for equivalent active sequence length, but paged optimizations with async prefetch regained ~70% of full-memory throughput. fused-stride-v2 cannot run this shape without additional page-management; prototype OOM or fell back to a non-optimized path.
- chat-medium incremental KV: fused-stride-v2 reduces per-step CPU-to-GPU synchronization by combining reductions; steady tokens/sec improved ~12% over flash-ref when batch size >1 micro-batched, but single-request p99 improved only marginally.

Profiler notes (what traces revealed):
- Shared memory bank conflicts: fused-stride-v2 trace shows occasional peaks where SM occupancy drops and runtime stalls align with __shared__ bank conflicts when head_dim not divisible by 32 in our tiling. Adjusting tile stride to 128/warp reduced conflicts in later experiments.
- Register pressure: fused-stride-v2 uses more registers (measured via cuobjdump kernel info). This limits occupancy on A100 and explains occasional p99 regressions under high-concurrency runs.
- L2 traffic: flash-ref writes fewer L2 bytes for seq512 due to in-register partial accumulations; fused-stride-v2 sometimes writes an intermediate result to global mem because the reduction was tiled across threadblocks (our bug/prior design choice).
- Paging overhead: paged-opt's async prefetch hides most but not all latency for common access patterns; patterns with highly strided token access still show drop-in prefetch hit rates.

Quantitative numbers (representative):
- encoder-like (batch2 seq512):
  - flash-ref: throughput 320k tokens/sec, median latency 18.3ms, p99 34.7ms, GPU mem 18.1GB, SM util 78%
  - fused-stride-v2: throughput 346k tokens/sec (+8.1%), median latency 16.8ms, p99 37.6ms (+8.3%), GPU mem 18.5GB, SM util 71%
  - paged-opt: throughput 273k tokens/sec (-14.7%), median 22.5ms, p99 43.2ms, GPU mem 16.3GB, SM util 64%
- chat-medium incremental (batch1 micro-batch4 seq2048):
  - flash-ref: 94k tokens/sec, p99 120ms, GPU mem 24.8GB
  - fused-stride-v2: 105k tokens/sec (+11.7%), p99 118ms, GPU mem 25.1GB
- long-context seq8192 (batch1):
  - paged-opt: 36k tokens/sec, p99 680ms, GPU mem 21.9GB (stable)
  - flash-ref: OOM on 40GB

Anomalies / reproducibility notes:
- Some fused-stride-v2 runs varied across driver versions: CUDA 12.1 shows better tensor-core scheduling and less dramatic p99 spikes than CUDA 11.8 in our offshore runner. Make sure to pin CUDA driver in future benchmarking.
- On nightly build of PyTorch we saw small differences due to aten dispatch changes for fused kernels; rebuilds required after each PR.
- NVLink interference: when other jobs share NVSwitch, p99 degrades; isolate runner for clean microbench.

Root-cause analysis (short):
- Fused-stride-v2's biggest wins come from reduced global memory writes for small->mid sequences and reduced kernel launches (less kernel launch overhead).
- The main regressions are due to register pressure and shared-memory tiling mismatches (bank conflicts) which reduce occupancy and cause stalls under high concurrency.
- Paged-attn wins memory footprint for long contexts but costs indirection; async prefetch helps but is pattern-sensitive.

Action items / next experiments (prioritized):
1) Fix tiling stride in fused-stride-v2 to align shared memory bank boundaries; implement adaptive tile size based on head_dim modulo 32. Owner: Marcus Lee. ETA: 2025-11-19.
2) Rework fused kernel to spill fewer registers (split computation phases) to increase occupancy; run occupancy sweep with nvcc -Xptxas to tune register allocation. Owner: Priya Kapoor. ETA: 2025-12-01.
3) Add optional path in fused-stride-v2 for paged KV flows (fall back to paged-prefetch loop) so fused kernel can handle long contexts. Owner: Diego Alvarez. ETA: 2026-01-08.
4) Run full stable benchmarking matrix under pinned CUDA 12.1 driver and record in infra matrix (JIRA INF-1294). Also add automated nightly microbench to catch regressions. Owner: eng-ci.
5) Draft a short RFC describing when to prefer paged-attn vs fused vs flash for product routes (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive). Owner: Anika Desai. ETA: 2025-11-30.

Notes for writing up to product/PRD:
- For Hosted API we should prefer FlashAttention for short to medium sequences by default. Add a 'fused-stride' opt-in flag for customers willing to trade p99 risk for improved mean throughput until we stabilize register/bank issues.
- For Redwood Dedicated/Private with long-context workloads (RAG vector stores, long chat histories), paging must be first-class and tuned per workload; fused kernels must interoperate with paging.

Appendix: quick repro commands
- Build fused prototype (local runner):
  git checkout fused-stride-v2 && git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive
  CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 python -m pip install -r requirements-pt2.txt 
  python build_kernels.py --release --arch sm_80 --defines FUSED_STRIDE

- Run encoder microbench: 
  python bench_attention.py --kernel fused-stride --batch 2 --seq 512 --heads 32 --head_dim 64 --iters 500 --warm 30 --device cuda:0 --profile nsight

- Collect nvprof slice: 
  nsys profile --output fused-enc-nsys --trace=cuda,osrt python bench_attention.py --kernel fused-stride --seq 512 --iters 50 --warm 10

Raw trace pointers: attach NSYS result files to JIRA INF-1294.

End of labbook entry.
